subject: Heteroskedasticity and Correlated Errors in Stan

messages.author: 8c4f70ab584cd6d9
messages.subject: Heteroskedasticity and Correlated Errors in Stan
parts:
I was curious if anyone has any experience with heteroskedasticity and correlated errors in Stan. Like a GLS approach.

For instance, consider Y generated from the R code below. What approach would be recommended assuming Y and X are known, but sigma and G are not?

I can do simple things like give the regression parameters a multivariate distribution, but I'm not sure if that is really sufficient in the presence of correlated errors. A multivariate normal distribution fit to Y doesn't make sense because if you fit it to cross-sectional data there's only one observation. Perhaps some kind of transformation?

N <- 1000
X <- rnorm(N, 0, 1)
G <- rnorm(N, 1, 0.1)

sigma <- G%*%t(G) + diag(rep(1, N))

Y <- X + rnorm(N, 0, 1) %*% chol(sigma)

parts:
This is what I have so far in my attempt at a transformation.

data {
    int<lower=0> N;
    vector[N] Y;
    vector[N] X;
}
transformed data {
    int<lower=1> N_upper;
    N_upper <- (N * (N - 1)) / 2;
}
parameters {
    real A;
    real B;
    vector[N_upper] inv_L_lower;
}
transformed parameters {
    cholesky_factor_cov[N] inv_L;
    vector[N] v;
   
    for (n in 1:N) {
        inv_L[n, n] <- 1;
    }
   
    {
        int i;
        i <- 1;
        for (m in 2:N) {
            for (j in 1:(m - 1)) {
                inv_L[m, j] <- inv_L_lower[i];
                inv_L[j, m] <- 0;
                i <- i + 1;
            }
        }
    }
   
    v <- inv_L' * Y;
}
model {
    A ~ normal(0, 10);
    B ~ normal(0, 10);
    v ~ normal(A + X * B, 1);
    increment_log_prob(log_determinant(inv_L'));

}
